sections.html:
• Common name: Highway Catfish
  • Described by Zheng, 1979
  • Size: 76 mm (3 in) SL
  • Temperature: 16.0–23.0°C
  • pH: 6.4–7.6
  • IUCN Red List: Not Evaluated
  • Etymology: the specific epithet comes from the Latin tres, meaning three, and linea, meaning line, in reference to the colour pattern.

Common name: Highway Catfish (no established Vietnamese name).

Family: Bagridae.

Synonyms: Pseudobagrus trilineatus, Leiocassis trilineatus.

Description: Dorsal spines (total): 2; dorsal soft rays (total): 7; anal soft rays: 18–19. Nude without scale, complete lateral line. Well developed dorsal fin, adipose fin about 1.4–2.8 times the length of the dorsal fin, nearly arc-shaped.

Colouration: Yellowish brown in colour, with three dark yellowish lateral stripes on the side (trilineatus). One of the stripes along the lateral line is discontinuous.

Size: 7.5 cm.
Dongjiang drainage (part of the Zhujiang [Pearl River] drainage) in southern China. Type locality: mountain stream in Luofu Shan, Boluo Xian, Guangdong Province, China.

Asia: China, Dongjiang basin. Type locality: Mountain stream in Luofu Shan, Boluo Xian, Guangdong Province, China.

IUCN Red List: This species occurs in the coastal rivers of Guangdong Province, China. The species has a stable population and is not impacted by significant threats. As such, it is assessed as Least Concern (IUCN 2024).
Found in hillstreams with moderate to swift current and a predominantly rocky bottom.
Males have an elongate genital papilla in front of the anal fin.
Unreported. There is but a single breeding report.

Tachysurus can be identified by an extrascapular without a laterosensory canal, and a pterotic with a broad lateral laminar expansion. It is among the most speciose catfish groups in East Asia and its members inhabit habitats ranging from fast-flowing hillstreams to large rivers.

Easily distinguished by its elongate body, long adipose fin and attractive colouration. Xanthic and albino forms exist.

Etymology: The genus name Tachysurus: tachys, swift; oura, tail, referring to the presumed agility of T. sinensis, based on its "long and nimble" tail (translation). The specific name trilineatus: tri-, three; lineatus, lined, referring to three yellowish lines on each side of the body.

Remarks: Still valid in some publications as Pseudobagrus trilineatus, but Eschmeyer's Catalog of Fishes has Tachysurus as the current genus name with Pseudobagrus trilineatus as a junior synonym.
